items.title: Putin calls Gulf leaders as Iran conflict widens

featured_image.name: In Russia, UAE leader calls for dialogue to end Ukraine war

items.description:
Russian President Vladimir Putin spoke by phone with UAE President Sheikh Mohammed bin Zayed Al Nahyan on Monday to discuss the rapidly escalating military conflict in the Middle East, as the Kremlin positioned itself as a potential mediator between Tehran and the Gulf states caught in the crossfire of U.S.-Israeli strikes on Iran.

The call, confirmed by the UAE state news agency WAM, came as Moscow said it remained in "constant contact" with Iran's leadership and was engaged in ongoing dialogue with Persian Gulf states affected by the widening conflict.[1][2]

items.title: Pentagon told Congress Iran showed no signs of attacking US first, sources say

featured_image.name: Pentagon Presses Iran Strike Claims as Briefed Senators ...

items.description:
The United States and Israel launched a sweeping joint military offensive against Iran on February 28, 2026, striking more than 1,000 targets across the country in what the Pentagon designated Operation Epic Fury and Israel called Operation Roaring Lion. The campaign killed Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei and dozens of senior officials, marking the most ambitious U.S.-Israeli military action in decades.[1][2]

As operations entered their third day on Monday, the assault showed no sign of slowing, with President Donald Trump warning that strikes could continue for "four weeks or as long as necessary". The Pentagon, however, faced mounting scrutiny after administration officials acknowledged in closed-door congressional briefings that there was no intelligence suggesting Iran had planned to attack U.S. forces first.[3][4][5]

items.title: Qatar shoots down two Iranian jets in Gulf first

featured_image.name: Qatar air force shoots down two aircraft from Iran: Defence ...

items.description:
Qatar's air force shot down two Iranian Sukhoi Su-24 fighter jets on Monday, marking the first time a Gulf country has engaged a manned Iranian aircraft since Tehran began its retaliatory bombardment of the region three days ago. The Qatari Defense Ministry said its forces also intercepted seven ballistic missiles and five drones, with all projectiles neutralized before reaching their intended targets.[1][2][3]

The shootdowns came on the third day of Iranian strikes across the Persian Gulf, launched in retaliation for joint US-Israeli attacks on Iran that killed Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei on February 28. Iran has targeted multiple Gulf states hosting US military assets, turning the skies over Doha, Dubai, Manama, and Kuwait City into active conflict zones.[4][5][6][7]

items.title: Trump says Iran war likely to last at least a month

featured_image.name: WATCH LIVE: Trump may address war with Iran at Medal of Honor ceremony

items.description:
President Trump used a Medal of Honor ceremony at the White House on Monday to deliver his first live public remarks on the U.S.-led military campaign against Iran, warning that operations could last four to five weeks and acknowledging that more American casualties are likely as the conflict enters its third day.[1][2]

The president spoke after awarding the Medal of Honor to three U.S. Army soldiers — Master Sergeant Roderick W. Edmonds, honored posthumously for protecting Jewish prisoners of war during World War II; Staff Sergeant Michael H. Ollis, honored posthumously for his heroism in Afghanistan; and Command Sergeant Major Terry P. Richardson, a retired Vietnam War veteran. The juxtaposition of honoring past military valor with the reality of a new armed conflict lent the ceremony an unusual gravity.[3][4]

items.title: Macron offers to station French nuclear weapons in Europe

featured_image.name: Reading between the lines of the new France-UK nuclear ...

items.description:
French President Emmanuel Macron declared on Monday that France will increase the size of its nuclear arsenal and strengthen its deterrence posture, warning that the world faces a growing risk of conflicts crossing the nuclear threshold. Speaking from the Île Longue submarine base in Brittany — home to France's four ballistic missile submarines — Macron described the current era as one of "geopolitical turmoil filled with dangers" and called for a "fortification" of France's deterrence.[1]

The address, closely watched by European allies, marks the most consequential shift in French nuclear doctrine in decades. Macron introduced a concept of "forward deterrence" and, for the first time, formally offered to station French nuclear weapons in other European nations, following a model long used by the United States, which maintains warheads in Germany, Belgium, Italy, and Turkey under NATO sharing arrangements.[2][3]

items.title: Trump pushes Venezuela model for Iran transition

featured_image.name: An Emboldened Trump Makes Big Bets in Venezuela, Iran and ...

items.description:
President Donald Trump said on March 1 that he envisions applying the political transition model used in Venezuela to post-Khamenei Iran, calling the Venezuelan operation "the perfect, the perfect scenario" in a phone interview with The New York Times.[1]

The remarks came days after U.S. and Israeli forces launched coordinated strikes against more than 1,000 sites across Iran on February 28, killing Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei and, according to Trump, eliminating much of Iran's military command. Trump announced Khamenei's death in a social media post hours after the operation began.[2][3]

items.title: Lebanon bans Hezbollah military operations after Israeli strikes kill dozens

featured_image.name: IDF and Hezbollah battle in Lebanon after Iran missile attack

items.description:
Lebanon's government on Monday banned all of Hezbollah's military and security operations, demanding the Iran-backed group hand over its weapons to the state after the militia's rocket and drone attacks on Israel triggered devastating retaliatory airstrikes that killed at least 31 people across the country.[1][2]

Prime Minister Nawaf Salam announced the decision following an emergency cabinet session, declaring that "any military or security action carried out from Lebanese territory outside the legitimate institutions" is unlawful. He urged Hezbollah to surrender its arms and said the Lebanese army would immediately begin implementing its plan to disarm the group north of the Litani River.[2][1]

items.title: Study: Climate pledges would still overshoot Paris 2°C target

featured_image.name: Despite Some Progress, Countries' New Climate Plans Largely Fall ...

items.description:
Even if every nation fulfills its current climate commitments, the world is still on track to warm by roughly 2.5°C — nearly half a degree above the Paris Agreement's 2°C safety threshold — according to a peer-reviewed study published in the journal Environmental Science & Policy.[1][2]

The research, led by Assistant Professor Taeyoung Jin of Jeonbuk National University in collaboration with Pusan National University, modeled climate and economic outcomes through the year 2300 using the Regional Integrated Model of Climate and the Economy (RICE-2010). The study projects that under a net-zero scenario reflecting current national pledges, global temperatures would rise approximately 2.48°C by 2300. Under a business-as-usual scenario with no emission cuts, warming could reach as high as 7°C over the same period.[3][2][4][1]
